conv_151.speaker: xX_Ottr_Mart_Xx
conv_151.text: Grain in {town} costs {gold} a sack now. Someone is gouging the road merchants, and it isn't me.

conv_151.speaker: Orrin_Chiselbeard
conv_151.text: Salt keeps its worth through a hard winter, Ottr, and so does a fair price. Steady hands win ground.

conv_151.speaker: xX_Ottr_Mart_Xx
conv_151.text: Fair price? My wagons sit idle with bandits on the road again. Terrible for trade, and I pay for the guards.

conv_151.speaker: Orrin_Chiselbeard
conv_151.text: Then carry less coin and hire fewer guards, Ottr. Honest salt at a fair rate needs no {troop_count} escorts.

conv_151.speaker: xX_Ottr_Mart_Xx
conv_151.text: Honest salt, says the man selling it at {gold} a barrel. Cheap talk, mentor.

conv_151.speaker: Orrin_Chiselbeard
conv_151.text: Mind your tongue at my table, Ottr. I have traded in {town} longer than you have owned a cart.

conv_151.speaker: xX_Ottr_Mart_Xx
conv_151.text: Then pay what the market pays and stop calling it charity. We will see who sells out first.

conv_152.speaker: bellwarden
conv_152.text: Word reached the council that {player} lost most of their {troop_count} soldiers near {town}. A grievous day. :(

conv_152.speaker: DameHingmere
conv_152.text: Most of their {troop_count}, gone in one afternoon. Hard to call that bad luck, Bellwarden.

conv_152.speaker: xX_EmberQuill_Xx
conv_152.text: I raise this matter before the council, {player}. An army lost so completely invites questions about who sent it marching.

conv_152.speaker: bellwarden
conv_152.text: Questions are cheap, Ember. {player} will need allies after a loss like that, and allies remember who asked first.

conv_152.speaker: DameHingmere
conv_152.text: {player}, a quiet word. The council will want it. My regency can offer shelter and {gold} to rebuild.

conv_152.speaker: bellwarden
conv_152.text: Generous offers cast long shadows, Hingmere. Let {player} rest before anyone asks them for more.

conv_152.speaker: xX_EmberQuill_Xx
conv_152.text: Rest is a fine notion, yet the matter stands before the council regardless. I shall wait to see who speaks first.

conv_153.speaker: xX_Crumbwright_Xx
conv_153.text: A cart went missing outside {village} this morning. The tracks lead off the old mill road. Curious, is it not? :)

conv_153.speaker: OldCloakwright
conv_153.text: Sit a while, {player}. The road will keep. A stolen cart is a lesson, not a ruin, and the tracks are still fresh.

conv_153.speaker: xX_Crumbwright_Xx
conv_153.text: Fresh tracks, you say. Interesting. Did {player} pass that mill road this morning, or did the cart roll off on its own?

conv_153.speaker: OldCloakwright
conv_153.text: I passed nothing but mud and a sleeping goat. Ask your own cart drivers, Crumbwright, before you point at honest folk.

conv_153.speaker: xX_Crumbwright_Xx
conv_153.text: Honest folk do not usually keep spare horseshoes in their wagons. But I shall let the magistrate decide who is honest.

conv_153.speaker: OldCloakwright
conv_153.text: Your suspicion grows heavy quickly, friend. Sit down with a cup of mulled cider and let the mud settle first.

conv_153.speaker: xX_Crumbwright_Xx
conv_153.text: Mulled cider while the cart is still missing. How very patient of you. Perhaps I shall check the mill road myself :)

conv_154.speaker: BaronBarrelcask
conv_154.text: {player} has defected to {faction}. A shame, for the salt contracts were nearly signed. Business is business, though.

conv_154.speaker: BaronBarrelcask
conv_154.text: Disloyal is a harsh word, Kabbage. Say rather the loyalty was for sale, and {faction} paid {gold} more.

conv_154.speaker: CountKabbage
conv_154.text: Loyalty is not a commodity. Those who sell it deserve what they get.

conv_154.speaker: BaronBarrelcask
conv_154.text: Business is business, {player}. Shall we talk prices before you sell that salt to {faction}?

conv_154.speaker: CountKabbage
conv_154.text: {player} will not last a season in {faction}. Their {troop_count} men are already grumbling.

conv_154.speaker: BaronBarrelcask
conv_154.text: Grumbling men make poor customers, Kabbage, but they still need salt for their stew. Mind your jibes, friend :)

conv_155.speaker: SirNutbrook
conv_155.text: Dear {player}, I should like a Word in council regarding the Iron prices in {town}. They are Outrageous.

conv_155.speaker: FactorAnvile
conv_155.text: Ha! Dear, maybe, but iron is dear this seaon :) Care for a deal on iron, {player}? Fair prices :)

conv_155.speaker: SirNutbrook
conv_155.text: Fair prices? Pah. Your Smiths gouge the {town} market and then Smile at us from behind their counters.

conv_155.speaker: FactorAnvile
conv_155.text: Gouge is a rough word, Nutbrook. My ledgers say otherwise, and the {village} folk agree :)

conv_155.speaker: SirNutbrook
conv_155.text: Your ledgers are Written by your own hand, Anvile. I should like to see the council audit them before spring.

conv_155.speaker: FactorAnvile
conv_155.text: Audit away! I'll bring the recipts and a basket of bread :) Good for the whole town, that.

conv_155.speaker: SirNutbrook
conv_155.text: Bread is no answer to {gold} for a bar of iron, Anvile. Pray the council is not so easily Charmed.
